\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Two-variable correlation matrix]
\lean{FABL.correlationMatrix}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p136-b008}
\label{FABL.correlationMatrix}
\leanok
For each real number $\rho$, define the matrix $C_\rho=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\
\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$, with rows and columns indexed by $\{0,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Factorization of the inverse correlation matrix]
\lean{FABL.exercise5_33a}
\label{FABL.exercise5_33a}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlationMatrix}
\difficulty{4}
For $-1<\rho<1$, let $R=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. Then
\[
R^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-\rho\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\0&(1-\rho^2)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&0\-\rho&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $-1<\rho<1$, $a\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$. For
$R=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $y=(\sigma a,\sigma a)^{\mathsf T}$,
the quadratic form satisfies
\[
y^{\mathsf T}R^{-1}y=\frac{2a^2}{1+\rho}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic form for opposite signs]
\lean{FABL.exercise5_33b_oppositeSigns}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p138-b003}
\label{FABL.exercise5_33b_oppositeSigns}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.exercise5_33a, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $-1<\rho<1$, $a\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$. For
$R=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $y=(\sigma a,-\sigma a)^{\mathsf T}$,
the quadratic form satisfies
\[
y^{\mathsf T}R^{-1}y=\frac{2a^2}{1-\rho}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive definiteness of the correlation matrix]
\lean{FABL.correlationMatrix_posDef}
\label{FABL.correlationMatrix_posDef}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlationMatrix}
\difficulty{5}
For every real number $\rho$ with $-1<\rho<1$, the matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ is positive definite.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlated sign summand]
\lean{FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand}
\label{FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
For a real number $c$ and a pair of signs $(u,v)\in\{\pm1\}^2$, define the corresponding
vector in $\mathbb R^2$ to have coordinates $(cu,cv)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Threshold pair summand]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand}
For a natural number $n$, a function $a:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb R$, an index
$i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and two points $x,y\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define the corresponding
vector in $\mathbb R^2$ to have coordinates $(a(i)x_i,a(i)y_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Regular threshold pair sum]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
For a natural number $n$, coefficients $a_i\in\mathbb{R}$ indexed by $i<n$, and a pair
$x,y\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the regular threshold pair sum is the vector in $\mathbb{R}^2$
obtained by summing, over all $i<n$, the corresponding regular threshold pair summand.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[First coordinate of the threshold pair sum]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_zero}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a_i\in\mathbb{R}$ for each $i<n$, and let $(x,y)$
be a pair of sign vectors of length $n$. The first coordinate of the sum of the vectors
$(a_i x_i,a_i y_i)$ over all $i<n$ is $\sum_{i<n}a_i x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second coordinate of the threshold pair sum]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_one}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a_i\in\mathbb{R}$ for each $i<n$, and let $(x,y)$
be a pair of sign vectors of length $n$. The second coordinate of the sum of the vectors
$(a_i x_i,a_i y_i)$ over all $i<n$ is $\sum_{i<n}a_i y_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Third-Moment Integrability of a Pair Summand]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $n$, any correlation parameter $\rho\in[-1,1]$, any coefficient
vector $a\colon\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb R$, and any coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
the corresponding two-dimensional summand is in $L^3$ with respect to the
correlated-pair distribution on the sign cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independence of correlated pair summands]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_iIndep}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_iIndep}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_pairCoordinatesEquiv, FABL.correlatedSignPairPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.independentProductPMF_toMeasure, FABL.pairCoordinatesEquiv, FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $a$ be a real coefficient
vector indexed by $i<n$. Draw a sign vector uniformly, then form a second sign vector by
independently, in each coordinate, keeping the first sign with probability $(1+\rho)/2$
and flipping it otherwise. Under this joint distribution, the random vectors $(a_i
x_i,a_i y_i)$, for $i<n$, are mutually independent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of one correlated pair summand]
\lean{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_expect_signValue_fst, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_expect_signValue_snd, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n$ be real
coefficients, and choose a coordinate $i$. Under the correlated sign-pair distribution
obtained by drawing a uniform sign vector and independently keeping each coordinate with
probability $(1+\rho)/2$ or flipping it otherwise, the expected vector $(a_i x_i,a_i
y_i)\in\mathbb R^2$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the correlated pair sum]
\lean{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSum_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSum_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_eq_zero, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n$ be real
coefficients. Draw a uniform sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, then form $y$ by
independently at each coordinate keeping $x_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and
flipping it otherwise. The expected value of the sum of vectors $(a_i x_i,a_i
y_i)\in\mathbb R^2$ over all coordinates $i$ is the zero vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Covariance of a regular correlated pair sum]
\lean{FABL.covarianceBilin_regularThresholdPairSum}
\label{FABL.covarianceBilin_regularThresholdPairSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.expect_linearForm_sq, FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSum_eq_zero, FABL.linearForm, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_fst, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_linearForm_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_snd, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}\in\mathbb
R$ satisfy $\sum_i a_i^2=1$. Choose a sign vector uniformly and, independently in each
coordinate, retain its sign with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and otherwise flip it; form
the pair sum whose $i$th contribution is $(a_i X_i,a_i Y_i)$. For all $x,y\in\mathbb
R^2$, the covariance bilinear form of this random pair sum satisfies
$\operatorname{Cov}(x,y)=x^{\mathsf T}\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Whitened norm as an inverse quadratic form]
\lean{FABL.bentkusWhitening_norm_sq_eq_inv_quadraticForm}
\label{FABL.bentkusWhitening_norm_sq_eq_inv_quadraticForm}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $d$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a positive definite real $d\times d$ matrix, and
let $z\in\mathbb R^d$. The squared Euclidean norm of $S^{-1/2}z$ equals the quadratic
form $z^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}z$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $-1<\rho<1$, let $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$. For the matrix
$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$, the Euclidean norm of
$\Sigma^{-1/2}(\varepsilon c,-\varepsilon c)$ is at most $\sqrt{2}\,|c|/\sqrt{1-\rho}$,
where $\Sigma^{-1/2}$ denotes the inverse of the positive square root of $\Sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Whitened Summand Norm Bound]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_norm_cube_le}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_norm_cube_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.bentkusWhitening_norm_oppositeSigns_le, FABL.bentkusWhitening_norm_sameSigns_le, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.regularCorrelatedSignSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in(-1,1)$, let $a$ be a real coefficient vector
on $n$ coordinates, let $i$ be one of those coordinates, and let $x,y\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The
cube of the norm of the summand after applying the inverse square root of the
correlation matrix is at most $(\sqrt{2}|a_i|/\sqrt{1+\rho})^3$ if $x_i=y_i$, and at
most $(\sqrt{2}|a_i|/\sqrt{1-\rho})^3$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement probability in a correlated sign pair]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_if_coordinate_signs_eq}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_if_coordinate_signs_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_expect_signValue_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, choose a coordinate
$i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let $u,v\in\mathbb{R}$. For a pair of sign vectors sampled
from the correlated pair distribution with parameter $\rho$, the expectation of the
function that equals $u$ when their signs agree at coordinate $i$ and $v$ otherwise is
$\frac{1+\rho}{2}u+\frac{1-\rho}{2}v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted cube scale bound]
\lean{FABL.weighted_whitening_scale_cube_le}
\label{FABL.weighted_whitening_scale_cube_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $\rho,c\in\mathbb{R}$ with $-1<\rho<1$. Then
\[\frac{1+\rho}{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}\,|c|}{\sqrt{1+\rho}}\right)^3+\frac{1-\rho}{2}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}\,|c|}{\sqrt{1-\rho}}\right)^3\leq\frac{4|c|^3}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Whitened third moment bound]
\lean{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le}
\label{FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.pmfExpectation_if_coordinate_signs_eq, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_norm_cube_le, FABL.weighted_whitening_scale_cube_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in(-1,1)$, let $a=(a_i)_{i=1}^n$ be real
coefficients, and choose a coordinate $i$. Under the correlated sign-pair distribution
with keep probability $(1+\rho)/2$, the expected cube of the Euclidean norm of the
vector obtained by applying the inverse square root of
$\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ to $(a_i x_i,a_i y_i)$ is at most
$\dfrac{4|a_i|^3}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Whitened correlated sign summands]
\lean{FABL.sum_integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le}
\label{FABL.sum_integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $-1<\rho<1$. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb
R$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$. Choose a
pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors in $\{\pm1\}^n$ by taking $x$ uniformly at random and,
independently in each coordinate, setting $y_i=x_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and
$y_i=-x_i$ otherwise. For each $i$, form $v_i=a_i(x_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^2$ and apply
the inverse positive square root of the matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. The sum over $i$ of the expected
cubed Euclidean norms of these transformed vectors is at most
$4\varepsilon/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Sign quadrant in the plane]
\lean{FABL.signQuadrant}
\label{FABL.signQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
For signs $s,t\in\{-1,1\}$, let $Q_{s,t}$ be the set of points
$z=(z_0,z_1)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying $s z_0\ge 0$ and $t z_1\ge 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Measurability of a sign-defined quadrant]
\lean{FABL.measurableSet_signQuadrant}
\label{FABL.measurableSet_signQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signQuadrant, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
For any two signs $s,t\in\{−1,1\}$, the set of points $(x_0,x_1)\in\mathbb R^2$
satisfying $0\le s x_0$ and $0\le t x_1$ is measurable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convexity of a sign quadrant]
\lean{FABL.isConvexSet_signQuadrant}
\label{FABL.isConvexSet_signQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signQuadrant, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s,t\in\{-1,1\}$, and consider the set of points $(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2$ satisfying
$sx\ge 0$ and $ty\ge 0$. This set is convex.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Correlation coordinates in Euclidean space]
\lean{FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\label{FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For a point $z=(z_1,z_2)$ in the correlation plane, its Euclidean coordinates are the
point $(z_1,z_2)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Euclidean coordinates in the correlation plane]
\lean{FABL.euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\label{FABL.euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane}
For a point $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, its correlation-plane coordinates are the
point $(z_1,z_2)$ in the correlation plane.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity of Euclidean coordinates]
\lean{FABL.continuous_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\label{FABL.continuous_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $z$ be a point of the real plane equipped with the $2$-norm. The map sending $z$ to
the Euclidean plane point with the same two real coordinates is continuous.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product under coordinate identification]
\lean{FABL.inner_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\label{FABL.inner_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
For every vector $z$ in the two-dimensional real correlation plane and every vector $t$
in the Euclidean plane, their inner product after identifying the correlation-plane
coordinates with Euclidean coordinates is unchanged when the identification is applied
to $t$ instead: $\langle z,t\rangle=\langle z,t\rangle$ under these respective
coordinate identifications.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic form in Euclidean coordinates]
\lean{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm_euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\label{FABL.correlationQuadraticForm_euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.euclideanCorrelationCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $\rho$ and every vector $t=(t_0,t_1)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, the
quadratic form $t_0^2+2\rho t_0t_1+t_1^2$ equals $t^{\mathsf
T}\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Euclidean form of the correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\label{FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.charFun_correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.continuous_correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure, FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.correlationMatrix_posDef, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm_euclideanCorrelationCoordinates, FABL.euclideanCorrelationCoordinates, FABL.inner_correlationEuclideanCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $-1<\rho<1$, and let $(X,Y)$ have the probability distribution obtained from
independent standard Gaussian variables $U,V$ by setting $X=U$ and $Y=\rho
U+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,V$. Under the identification of the plane with $\mathbb R^2$, this
distribution is the multivariate Gaussian with mean $(0,0)$ and covariance matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian lower-left quadrant probability]
\lean{FABL.multivariateGaussian_lowerLeftQuadrant}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p120-b003
}
\label{FABL.multivariateGaussian_lowerLeftQuadrant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.continuous_correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.correlatedGaussianMeasure_map_correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.correlationEuclideanCoordinates, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.measurableSet_signQuadrant, FABL.sheppardsFormula, FABL.signQuadrant}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\rho\in(-1,1)$, and consider the centered bivariate Gaussian distribution with
covariance matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. The probability that
both coordinates are nonpositive is $\frac12-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\arccos(\rho)}{\pi}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform Gaussian approximation for regular thresholds]
\lean{FABL.exists_exercise5_33c_constant}
\label{FABL.exists_exercise5_33c_constant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationMatrix, FABL.correlationMatrix_posDef, FABL.covarianceBilin_regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_eq_zero, FABL.isConvexSet_signQuadrant, FABL.measurableSet_signQuadrant, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_iIndep, FABL.regularThresholdPairSummand_memLp, FABL.signQuadrant, FABL.sum_integral_regularThresholdPairSummand_whitening_cube_le}
\difficulty{4}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. For every dimension $n$, every
$\rho\in(-1,1)$, every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb
R^n$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, and every pair of
signs $s,t$, the absolute difference between the probability that the correlated random
sign vectors’ weighted sum lies in the quadrant determined by $s,t$ and the
corresponding centered Gaussian probability with covariance matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ is at most $C\varepsilon/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign reversal of a linear form]
\lean{FABL.linearForm_neg_input_regularThreshold}
\label{FABL.linearForm_neg_input_regularThreshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and every
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, negating all coordinates of $x$ negates the linear form:
$L_a(-x)=-L_a(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonvanishing of a balanced threshold form]
\lean{FABL.homogeneousThreshold_linearForm_ne_zero_of_balanced}
\label{FABL.homogeneousThreshold_linearForm_ne_zero_of_balanced}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.linearForm, FABL.linearForm_neg_input_regularThreshold, FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_neg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$, and let $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$.
Suppose the mean of the real-valued version of $f$ on the uniform sign cube is zero, and
$f(x)$ equals the threshold sign of $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ for every $x$. Then
$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\ne 0$ for every sign vector $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Negative threshold characterization]
\lean{FABL.homogeneousThreshold_eq_neg_one_iff}
\label{FABL.homogeneousThreshold_eq_neg_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.linearForm, FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_of_neg, FABL.thresholdSign_of_nonneg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$, and let $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$.
Suppose that for every sign vector $x$, $f(x)$ is the sign determined by the threshold
at the linear form $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$. Then $f(x)=-1$ if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^n
a_i x_i<0$, for every $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower-left quadrant characterization]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_mem_lowerLeft_iff}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_mem_lowerLeft_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.homogeneousThreshold_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.linearForm, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_one, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_apply_zero, FABL.signQuadrant, FABL.signValue_neg_one, FABL.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from sign vectors of length $n$
to signs, and let $a$ be a real coefficient vector. Suppose $f(x)$ is the sign of
$\sum_{i<n}a_i x_i$ for every sign vector $x$, and this sum is never zero. For every
pair $(x,y)$ of sign vectors, the vector $\sum_{i<n}(a_i x_i,a_i y_i)$ lies in the
lower-left quadrant if and only if $f(x)=f(y)=-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower-Left Probability as an Acceptance Expectation]
\lean{FABL.regularThresholdPair_lowerLeftProbability_eq}
\label{FABL.regularThresholdPair_lowerLeftProbability_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.linearForm, FABL.measurableSet_signQuadrant, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_eq_integral, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum, FABL.regularThresholdPairSum_mem_lowerLeft_iff, FABL.signQuadrant, FABL.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be
a sign-valued Boolean function, and let $a$ be a real coefficient vector on $n$
coordinates. Suppose $f(x)$ is the sign of the linear form with coefficients $a$ for
every $x$, and that this linear form is nonzero at every $x$. Under the correlated-pair
distribution, the probability that the sum of the pair summands lies in the quadrant
with both coordinates nonpositive, converted to a real number, equals the expectation of
the indicator that both function values are $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise stability and the lower-left probability]
\lean{FABL.noiseStability_eq_four_mul_lowerLeftProbability_sub_one}
\label{FABL.noiseStability_eq_four_mul_lowerLeftProbability_sub_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsBalanced, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.noiseStability, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_fst, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_snd, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$
be a Boolean function whose mean under the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}^n$ is zero.
Form a random pair $(X,Y)$ by choosing $X$ uniformly and, independently in each
coordinate, setting $Y_i=X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=-X_i$ otherwise.
Then the noise stability satisfies $\mathbb{E}[f(X)f(Y)]=4\,\mathbb{P}(f(X)=-1\text{ and
}f(Y)=-1)-1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. For every natural number $n$,
every Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, every coefficient vector
$a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, every real number $\varepsilon$, and every $-1<\rho<1$, suppose that
$f$ has mean zero, $f(x)$ is the sign of the homogeneous linear form $\sum_i a_i x_i$
for every $x$, $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every coordinate $i$.
Then the absolute difference between the noise stability of $f$ at correlation $\rho$
and $\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\rho)$ is at most $\frac{C\varepsilon}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}$.
\end{theorem}
